properties.decision: PROPOSED (my recommendation, built so Anthony can veto before merge): (C) the server-time stamps and their seal live in the store. export_graph carries them only with a new opt-in `stamps: true` (additive); the one-file-per-item layout and the design copy in git never carry them. The prediction-order reading runs where the stamps were recorded (the live design on flo2.io, a --call copy of the store, a moved store directory); an opt-in export imported elsewhere reads "imported, not recorded here". Alternatives: (A) stamps in every export and the design copy — breaks 4 core tests, chiefly two PRs that each accept a checksum on one Artifact would conflict on that item file again (the conflict the per-item layout exists to prevent), and identical designs would stop exporting identically; (B) never export them — C without the opt-in, so a backup or move by export would lose every stamp.
properties.name: Write stamps stay in the store; an export carries them only when asked, and the design copy never does
properties.rationale: Measured by the gap-3 build 2026-10-28 (local commit 037a2dfda): with stamps in exports, the_design_is_saved_one_file_per_item (two branches accepting one file each), a changed-then-restored item leaving no diff, two exports of an unchanged graph byte-identical, and stale_seat's unchanged-design check all fail. The hash chain cannot vouch for a stamp (content_hash is unkeyed); only the store's HMAC seal does, and only to the store holding the key, so carrying stamps in git copies would add churn without trust. Follows dec:prediction-order-is-read-from-server-recorded-times-and-said-not-enforced-2026-10-28. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018ibUbMKCS1yK5W17cncp9P
